beats.text: In the late 1970s, geophysicists Glen Penfield and Antonio Camargo discovered a mysterious ring beneath the Yucatán Peninsula.
beats.say: In the late 1970s, geophysicists Glen Penfield and Antonio Camargo discovered a mysterious ring beneath the Yucatán Peninsula.

beats.text: Penfield noted anomalies suggesting an impact feature, but Pemex rejected the crater theory.
beats.say: Penfield noted anomalies suggesting an impact feature, but Pemex rejected the crater theory.

beats.text: In 1990, Alan R. Hildebrand and Glen Penfield identified the Chicxulub crater, named after the nearby town.
beats.say: In 1990, Alan R. Hildebrand and Glen Penfield identified the Chicxulub crater, named after the nearby town.

beats.text: The crater, 200 km wide, was formed 66 million years ago, coinciding with the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction.
beats.say: The crater, two hundred kilometers wide, was formed sixty-six million years ago, coinciding with the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction.

beats.text: Impact evidence includes shocked quartz, tektites, and a gravity anomaly, supporting the asteroid impact theory.
beats.say: Impact evidence includes shocked quartz, tektites, and a gravity anomaly, supporting the asteroid impact theory.

beats.text: Today, the Chicxulub crater is recognized as the primary cause of the K–Pg extinction event, leading to the demise of 75% of life on Earth.
beats.say: Today, the Chicxulub crater is recognized as the primary cause of the K–Pg extinction event, leading to the demise of seventy-five percent of life on Earth.
